meta.source: Computed by npm run build:data from data/peak-hour-demand.json, data/fhr-to-tank-size.json, data/energystar-water-heaters.json and data/household-size-guides.json with assets/js/formulas.js
meta.notes: Default result, household table, worked example and manufacturer cross-check for the tank size calculator.

default.statusLabel: The typical size: meets the median of 4 models in our sample
default.headline: 50-gallon gas tank (first hour rating 69+ gal)
default.explain: Your busiest hour uses about 69 gallons of hot water, so choose a heater with a first hour rating (FHR) of at least 69 gallons. Other fuels: 55-gallon electric (typical first hour rating 74 gal); 65-gallon heat pump (typical first hour rating 75 gal). American Water Heater suggests an FHR of 62–74 gal for 4 people; your busy hour is inside that range (our household presets are set to land in it, so this is a consistency check; Rheem and A. O. Smith are the independent ones on Methodology).
default.formula:
Peak-hour demand = 3 × 20 gal (shower) + 1 × 4 gal (hands and face washing) + 1 × 5 gal (food preparation) = 69 gal
Required FHR = 69 × 1 = 69 gal (rounded up)
Gas: 50 gal; that size rates 75–86 gal, typical 81 (4 models)
Electric: 55 gal; that size rates 74–74 gal, typical 74 (1 model)
Heat pump: 65 gal; that size rates 54–82 gal, typical 75 (24 models)
default.sources: Per-use gallons: AHRI peak-hour worksheet. First hour ratings: Rheem spec sheets (gas, electric) and the ENERGY STAR certified list (heat pump). The 4-person busy hour is our assumption; change the counts. See our results checked against American, Rheem and A. O. Smith sizing guides.
